experiment_recipes.goal: Verify that the operating conditions are explicitly defined and that the learned discrete-time dynamics model is non-vacuously predictive before testing any error bound
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: state-action transition learning for dynamics models
metrics: one-step-ahead prediction error / mean squared error
model prediction or dynamics approximation error
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using 10000 training transitions sampled inside the declared operating box and 2000 independent validation transitions from the same condition, the GP one-step state-difference predictor must achieve validation MSE <= 0.50 times the MSE of a zero-order-hold predictor and 100% of validation state-action pairs must lie inside the declared operating box. Failure of either condition refutes the claim for this operating condition/data regime because the prerequisite learned dynamics system is not established.
constraints_not_enforced: Does not test the error bound itself
Does not test statistical-confidence coverage
Does not test long-horizon or trajectory-wise always-overestimating behavior
Does not test real robotic data
experiment_recipes.rationale: A cheap system-identification prerequisite is to check that the learned dynamics model has non-trivial one-step predictive skill on independent data drawn from the stated operating condition.

experiment_recipes.goal: Construct and validate a non-trivial statistical error model for the learned dynamics model
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Fit a 95% one-step Euclidean prediction-error bound b(x,u) from the GP predictive uncertainty using a calibration split, then evaluate on a separate apparatus-validation split of at least 5000 transitions. Pass only if empirical pointwise coverage Pr(||x_{t+1}-xhat_{t+1}||_2 <= b(x_t,u_t)) is >= 0.95 and the median bound is <= 0.50 times the operating-box one-step state-difference diameter. If coverage is < 0.95, or if the bound is larger than this non-triviality threshold, the apparatus is invalid.
constraints_not_enforced: Does not establish trajectory-wise always-overestimating behavior
Does not establish coverage on real robotic systems
Does not prove validity outside the declared operating box
Uses 95% as the tested statistical confidence level
depends_on: Verify that the operating conditions are explicitly defined and that the learned discrete-time dynamics model is non-vacuously predictive before testing any error bound
experiment_recipes.rationale: Uncertainty-bound validation on an independent split is the standard statistical-learning check that the fitted error model is both calibrated and not merely a vacuous worst-case bound.

experiment_recipes.goal: Directly test whether the learned error model overestimates the true discrete-time dynamics error with the claimed statistical confidence on independent simulated trajectories
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: On 1000 independent test trajectories of length 200 with uniformly sampled initial conditions and admissible controls inside the declared operating box, mark a trajectory successful only if ||x_{t+1}-xhat_{t+1}||_2 <= b(x_t,u_t) for every time step t. Pass only if the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower confidence bound on the successful-trajectory probability is >= 0.95 and the median per-step bound remains <= 0.50 times the operating-box one-step state-difference diameter. Any violation of the lower-confidence-bound criterion refutes the always-overestimates-up-to-statistical-confidence claim for this condition.
constraints_not_enforced: Does not exhaustively quantify over every continuous state-action point between sampled trajectories
Does not test physical robot measurement noise
Does not test confidence levels other than 95%
Does not test operating conditions outside the declared box
depends_on: Construct and validate a non-trivial statistical error model for the learned dynamics model
experiment_recipes.rationale: The claim's central assertion is simultaneous overestimation of true error with statistical confidence; trajectory-level coverage is the standard direct Monte Carlo validation for discrete-time learned dynamics.

experiment_recipes.goal: Test the same statistical error-bound claim on robotic manipulator data rather than only on a simulated benchmark
experiment_recipes.dataset: simulated and real seven-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator data
metrics: model prediction or dynamics approximation error
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train the Bayesian neural-network dynamics model on the training portion of the manipulator transition data, fit a 95% error bound using a calibration split, and evaluate on held-out validation trajectories. A trajectory is successful only if the observed one-step Euclidean prediction error is <= the predicted error bound at every step. Pass only if the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower confidence bound on successful-trajectory probability is >= 0.95 and the median bound is <= 0.75 times the median bound of the trivial operating-range diameter bound. Otherwise refute the claim for this robotic-data operating condition.
constraints_not_enforced: Uses observed transition error as the true error, not an unobserved noise-free latent dynamics error
Does not test every possible robotic platform
Does not test operating conditions outside the recorded manipulator regime
Uses 95% as the tested statistical confidence level
depends_on: Construct and validate a non-trivial statistical error model for the learned dynamics model
experiment_recipes.rationale: A real robotic manipulator dataset is a standard model-based-RL/system-identification setting; validating uncertainty bounds on held-out trajectories tests whether the claim survives realistic robotic data rather than only simulation.

experiment_recipes.goal: Show that successful coverage is attributable to the learned non-trivial error model rather than to arbitrary conservative widening or random bounds
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Repeat the headline simulated-trajectory test with two matched-budget ablations: (i) replace b(x,u) by a constant bound equal to the full model's median bound, and (ii) randomly permute b(x,u) across test state-action pairs, preserving the same bound distribution. The control passes only if the full learned error model has one-sided 95% lower successful-trajectory coverage >= 0.95, while each ablation either has lower confidence bound < 0.95 or has empirical successful-trajectory coverage at least 5 percentage points below the full model at the same median bound. If ablations also satisfy the same coverage and tightness criteria, the mechanism-specific claim is not supported.
constraints_not_enforced: Does not compare against every possible alternative uncertainty method
Does not test real robotic data
Does not prove validity outside sampled operating conditions
depends_on: Directly test whether the learned error model overestimates the true discrete-time dynamics error with the claimed statistical confidence on independent simulated trajectories
experiment_recipes.rationale: Ablating the state/action-dependent learned error model while matching bound size tests whether the result is caused by the claimed error-model mechanism rather than by vacuous conservatism or chance.

experiment_recipes.goal: Check the claim's sufficient-data dependence by sweeping data size and verifying that valid non-trivial bounds emerge only when enough data are provided
metrics: one-step-ahead prediction error / mean squared error
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Train and calibrate the same GP dynamics/error-bound pipeline with n in {500, 2000, 10000, 50000} transitions, using identical operating conditions and independent 1000-trajectory test sets. Pass only if there exists at least one n <= 50000 for which the one-sided 95% lower successful-trajectory coverage is >= 0.95 and the median bound is <= 0.50 times the operating-box one-step state-difference diameter, and if increasing n from 500 to that passing n reduces validation MSE by at least 25%. If no tested data size reaches the coverage and non-triviality thresholds, the sufficient-data claim is refuted for this benchmark and data budget.
constraints_not_enforced: Does not prove that some larger untested data size could not eventually pass
Does not test all robotic systems
Does not test outside the declared operating box
Uses 95% as the tested statistical confidence level
depends_on: Directly test whether the learned error model overestimates the true discrete-time dynamics error with the claimed statistical confidence on independent simulated trajectories
experiment_recipes.rationale: Statistical learning theory expects uncertainty validity and tightness to improve with sample size; a sample-complexity sweep checks the claim's explicit sufficient-data qualifier.
